claim: Acquire the public repository epachayan/indus-script at commit 5c14a01f44296a01256a34e7e5e5e9fd82d9a67f and record what its seal tables contain. Mackay (1938) and Marshall (1931) each printed a table of the seals from their excavations at Mohenjo-daro. The repository's README describes a 709-row transcription of Mackay's "Tabulation of Seals" (type, size in inches, material, block, house and room or street, level relative to the DK datum, and field number) and a 560-row transcription of Marshall's table (type, size, material, excavation area and depth below the surface), both checked against a separate OCR reading. A datum is the fixed reference height from which an excavator measured levels, and a field number is the number given to a find when it was excavated. A Zenodo record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23281781, CC BY 4.0) describes the same work; its version note says an AI model produced the tables, and the record holds only a preprint PDF, so the repository is the data source.
title: Acquire the machine-readable Mackay 1938 and Marshall 1931 seal tables at a pinned commit
